description: Each status's count is the number of scan records linked to sites with that status.

c.request: Matching scans to their sites (`scans.zoneref` = `sites.zoneregistry`, skipping unmatched scans) and grouping by the sites' health and safety status (`sites.healtheval`), take the statuses whose average file size per minute (`gbsize` ÷ `spanmin`, ignoring missing values) is above the average across all statuses (none if that average is missing). In one unrounded row, what is their average rate, what is their average count, and on average how far does their rate exceed the all-status average? Each status's count is the number of scan records linked to sites with that status.
c.sql: WITH status_rates AS (SELECT si.healtheval, AVG(sc.gbsize / NULLIF(sc.spanmin, 0)) AS avg_rate, COUNT(*) AS scan_count FROM scans AS sc JOIN sites AS si ON sc.zoneref = si.zoneregistry GROUP BY si.healtheval), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_rate) AS all_status_avg_rate FROM status_rates) SELECT AVG(sr.avg_rate) AS average_rate, AVG(sr.scan_count) AS average_count, AVG(sr.avg_rate - o.all_status_avg_rate) AS average_excess_rate FROM status_rates AS sr CROSS JOIN overall AS o WHERE sr.avg_rate > o.all_status_avg_rate;

b.request: Join scans to matching sites, group by health and safety status, and count all linked scan records in each group. For each status, average the nonmissing scan-level `gbsize / spanmin` rates; select statuses whose rate exceeds the average of those status rates, or none if that overall average is missing. Return one unrounded row containing the selected statuses’ average rate, average scan count, and average excess rate over the overall average
b.sql: WITH status_rates AS (SELECT si.healtheval AS health_safety_status, COUNT(*) AS scan_count, AVG(sc.gbsize / NULLIF(sc.spanmin, 0)) AS avg_rate FROM scans AS sc JOIN sites AS si ON si.zoneregistry = sc.zoneref GROUP BY si.healtheval), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_rate) AS overall_avg_rate FROM status_rates) SELECT AVG(sr.avg_rate) AS avg_rate, AVG(sr.scan_count) AS avg_scan_count, AVG(sr.avg_rate - o.overall_avg_rate) AS avg_excess_rate FROM status_rates AS sr CROSS JOIN overall AS o WHERE sr.avg_rate > o.overall_avg_rate;

a.request: Match each scan to its site (`scans.zoneref` = `sites.zoneregistry`), dropping unmatched scans, and group by the site's health and safety status (`healtheval`). For each status, work out the average file size per minute (`gbsize` ÷ `spanmin`, ignoring missing values) and the number of scans. Keep the statuses whose rate is above the average rate across all statuses (none if that average is missing). Then give one unrounded row: the average rate of those statuses, their average number of scans, and the average amount by which their rate exceeds the all-status average.
a.sql: WITH status_rates AS (SELECT s.healtheval, AVG(sc.gbsize / NULLIF(sc.spanmin, 0)) AS rate, COUNT(*) AS scan_count FROM scans AS sc JOIN sites AS s ON sc.zoneref = s.zoneregistry GROUP BY s.healtheval), all_statuses AS (SELECT AVG(rate) AS average_rate FROM status_rates) SELECT AVG(sr.rate) AS average_rate, AVG(sr.scan_count) AS average_scan_count, AVG(sr.rate - a.average_rate) AS average_excess_rate FROM status_rates AS sr CROSS JOIN all_statuses AS a WHERE sr.rate > a.average_rate

d.request: Match scans to sites where `scans.zoneref = sites.zoneregistry`, excluding unmatched scans. Group the matched scans by `sites.healtheval`. For each status, calculate its average file size per minute as the average of `gbsize ÷ spanmin`, ignoring missing values, and count the scan records linked to sites with that status. Select statuses whose average rate exceeds the average rate across all statuses; select none if the all-status average is missing. In one unrounded row, what are the selected statuses’ average rate, average scan count, and average amount by which their rates exceed the all-status average?
d.sql: WITH status_rates AS (SELECT sites.healtheval AS status, AVG(scans.gbsize / NULLIF(scans.spanmin, 0)) AS average_rate, COUNT(*) AS scan_count FROM scans JOIN sites ON scans.zoneref = sites.zoneregistry GROUP BY sites.healtheval), all_statuses AS (SELECT AVG(average_rate) AS average_rate FROM status_rates) SELECT AVG(sr.average_rate) AS average_rate, AVG(sr.scan_count) AS average_scan_count, AVG(sr.average_rate - a.average_rate) AS average_excess_rate FROM status_rates AS sr CROSS JOIN all_statuses AS a WHERE sr.average_rate > a.average_rate HAVING COUNT(*) > 0;
